cards.front: Recall a key point about Sawm: Fasting
cards.back: Sawm (fasting) during Ramadan is the third Pillar of Islam. Muslims do not eat, drink, smoke or engage in sexual activity from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib) for the entire month of Ramadan — the month when the Qur'an was first revealed to Muhammad.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: In the UK, summer Ramadan fasting days can last over 18 hours, from approximately 2:30am to 9:30pm. Despite this extreme challenge, surveys show that over 90% of British Muslims fast during Ramadan, with many reporting that the spiritual benefits far outweigh the physical difficulty.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, British Muslims faced the unusual challenge of fasting during Ramadan while mosques were closed. Communities adapted by organising virtual iftars, online tarawih prayers and contactless food distribution to those in need, demonstrating how the spirit of Ramadan could be maintained even under extreme restrictions.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: In 2024, the Muslim Council of Britain issued guidance to schools on supporting fasting students during exam season, recommending that schools provide quiet rest areas, allow students to avoid strenuous PE activities, and schedule important exams for the morning when fasting students have more energy. This reflects the growing recognition of Ramadan as an important part of British life.
